author: Temminck & Schlegel, 1849
status: 겨울철새, 해마다 수백 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 탁 트인 들에 사는 새로, 우리나라에서는 흔히 겨울을 나는 겨울철새이면서 드물게 번식하는 여름철새이기도 하다. 번식기에는 일부일처로 지내며, 땅을 오목하게 파고 마른풀을 깔아 둥지를 지은 뒤 엷은 황회색 바탕에 어두운 갈색 얼룩이 있는 알을 낳는다. 짧은 날개를 빠르게 저어 곧게 날지만 멀리 가지는 못하고 약 50m쯤 날아간다. 전국에 살며 국외에서는 유라시아 대륙과 아프리카에 분포한다.

art.subject: Japanese Quail (Coturnix japonica), adult male in winter, as seen in open Korean fields from October to March: forehead, crown and nape blackish with broad rufous-brown feather edges and a narrow pale central crown stripe; long white supercilium running from the bill base to the nape; face and throat pale buff to rusty; neck, mantle, rump and uppertail coverts rusty with small black triangular feather tips; back and scapulars buff-brown heavily streaked with long creamy-white shaft streaks and black bars; breast warm rufous-buff; flanks rufous with long pale streaks; belly buffy-white, paler than the back. Bill short, grey-brown, blackish near the tip; iris brown; legs pale flesh.
art.pose: crouching on the ground among dry grass, side view

views: adult male winter, side view standing in grass: blackish crown with rufous fringes and a pale central stripe, long white supercilium to the nape, rusty neck with small black triangular spots, buff-brown back streaked white and black, rufous-buff breast and streaked flanks, pale belly, pale flesh legs
adult, head detail in side view: short grey-brown bill blackish near the tip, white supercilium reaching the nape, striped crown
art.build: Small, rotund ground bird, 20cm, clearly bigger than a sparrow but far smaller than a pheasant; shaped like a plump egg with a small head, no crest and almost no visible tail. Bill short and stout, chicken-like with a curved culmen, much shorter than the head. Legs short, pale flesh. Crouches and runs in grass rather than flying. At rest the short rounded wings cover the flanks and the tiny tail is hidden among the rump feathers. When flushed it flies low and straight on rapidly whirring short wings for a short distance, then drops back into cover.
avoid: Do not draw a crest, head plume or visible tail.
Do not paint a bold black-and-white throat pattern or a plain grey face; the head is buff and rufous with a white supercilium.
Do not make it partridge- or pheasant-sized; it is a tiny, round quail.
Do not paint grey or dark legs; they are pale flesh.
